items.title: Seats kept on first connect, given up when evicted
items.box:
Seats kept on first connect; an evicted node told so in Natter.

FOUND (tree at f0d03916, 2026-10-12; paths under spirit/run/)
- HIGH: the first stream to a new relay erases the seat the claim just wrote (js/hub.js seats, js/answerRelay.js calls relayKeys.accept on a "new" verdict, js/relayKeys.js rewrites the whole row). Every new node reads "You (unknown)"; test/presenceProof.js never checks the label.
- HIGH: a seat is never given up: relayKeys.unseat has no caller; any pin counts as a seat; ownerBadge claimed = owned || hasSeat; natterDetails hides the claim form.
- An owner can evict (Contacts details > Forget twice sends removePeer to each relay). The evicted node is never told, keeps its seat, and can never re-claim.
- MEDIUM: a re-claim answered 409 for the node's own key records no seat (hub.js).
- MEDIUM: the seat label is frozen at claim time (ownerBadge); a rename from Info never re-seats.
- LOW: natterDetails reads c.peers and roll.roster; the probe sets neither.

DECIDED (Andy, 2026-10-12; the chat holds every line)
- The relay has no power over a member node's data; only the node's user removes a relay, never the last one. "Nobody other than the node user has a right to remove data". A relay must withstand repeated denied requests.
- The eviction stands and frees the slot; "the seat is already vacated, so the nodes ID has to get a new invite, that what the info in natter is supposed to convey." No try-again; re-admission is a new invite, arranged off the wire.
- "it happens all behind peerPost, when a rejection-reply arrives and peerPost stashes the info into the relay table, from then on peerPost will reject posts to that relay. simple, no interventions needed, natter will know from being allows access to the relay table. and peerPost streams the rejection for realtime update to shell."
- "we don't cheat at the first opportunity" / "peerPost, on receiving and recognizing the FUCKING rejection, terminate the correct ONE relayStream that belongs to the rejecting relay." / "at the same point it writes to the relay-row"
- The refusal names the sender, not the recipient: "your id is not a valid sender here" (code not-a-sender), on the post, the reply and the stream.
- One door first: goal/G19.14 (closed) put the node's relay streams behind peerPost.

SHAPE
- relayKeys.accept merges instead of replacing; a 409 re-claim of its own key seats as on a 2xx.
- peerPost, at the one place it recognises a not-a-sender reply: writes the rejection and its time into that relay's row in the relay table, closes exactly that relay's stream (it keeps each stream's handle, handing presenceNode the opener; presenceNode unchanged), refuses every later post to that relay, and streams the rejection to the shell.
- A start or restart does not open a stream to a relay whose row holds a rejection (the list comes from ownerBadge).
- Natter reads the relay table: on that relay's row it says the relay refused this node, since when, that the seat is gone and only a new invite brings it back, and offers the user's Remove (never on the last relay). Remove gives up the seat (relayKeys.unseat, its first caller).
- The LOW reads in natterDetails are fixed with the code this item changes.
- Rename: no new verb. Info already tells every relay the new name through peerPost ("you node will notify the relays, through peerPost"); peerPost, when a relay accepts the rename, writes the new label into that relay's row (relay-state/relayKeys.json, through relayKeys), at the same door as the rejection ("yes.", Q19).

GRANTS: G1 (hub, answerRelay, relayKeys, ownerBadge, natter, natterDetails, info) and G3 (peerPost, relay, spiritErrors).

Asked where the rejection is kept: "the authoritative info about relays on the node MUST be by ID (key)"

On the listening line: "understood. granted. for now." So relayServer says the real reason when it refuses a stream, sseClient passes it on, and peerPost recognises the not-a-sender refusal on the stream too and stops that redial.

Three of the four parts have one plain answer each:
- first connect: relayKeys.accept merges into the row instead of replacing it, so the seat the claim wrote survives;
- 409 re-claim of its own key: the node writes the seat as on a 2xx, with the relay's label for it;
- rename: a rename from Info writes the seat label again.
The fourth is a design point: when you Forget a member, the relay drops it, but the node never learns, keeps its seat and dials forever.
My proposal: no new wire verb. The relay already refuses an unknown key's stream; on that refusal the node gives up its seat (relayKeys.unseat), and its claim form shows again so it can be invited back.
Should an evicted node give up its seat on the relay's refusal, as proposed?
Checked: the relay does refuse a forgotten key's stream, 403 "no such identity" (js/relay.js:4668, streamOpen), so the node has a clear signal to give up its seat on.

Q1: Should an evicted node give up its seat on the relay's refusal, as proposed?

isn't it just evicted, and it's future tries to connect will be rejected?

On the relay, yes: it is out, and every try is refused. The trouble is the evicted node's own view: it still believes it is a member, so it dials that relay again and again forever, its Natter shows it as claimed, and the claim form stays hidden, so even if you invite it back it cannot join. Giving up its seat on the refusal is only the node catching up with what the relay already decided.

the relay, by definition, has no power over a member-node's data, so the only thing that could be done: help a node realize it is outcast, and remove that relay from it's list.

thoughts?

That is the same thing said better: the relay decides membership, the node only stops pretending. On a stream refused "no such identity" the node gives up its seat, takes that relay off its list, stops dialing it, and says so where you will see it (a line in Natter: removed from <relay>), never silently.
One caveat: a relay that lost its roll (restored from an old copy) refuses the same way, and the node cannot tell the two apart; either way the membership is gone, and an invite brings it back.
Shall I write it into the box like that?

a relay row may need a field, that persists the rejection, until the user sees that in natter, and removes the relay himself, the automation of a removal may exceed our (coders) authority. Nobody other than the node user has a right to remove data:

furthermore, the user may call the relay-owner by phone and clear up misunderstandings that lead to the eviction in the first place....

also: a relay MUST be robust to malicious attacks, and repeating denied request might only be ignorance, not maliciousness.
